name: Preference would rather
pattern: VP[would rather + plain infinitival or finite subordinate clause]

entry.name: Preference would rather
entry.pattern: VP[would rather + plain infinitival or finite subordinate clause]

1.definition: Expresses preference between actual or imagined alternatives.

projection.target: A finite clause can have its own subject and a modally remote preterite. In I would rather stay, the subject of stay is understood as the matrix subject.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Saying what you would prefer
curious.summary: Would rather expresses a preference between real or imagined alternatives, and can be followed by a plain verb or a whole clause.
curious.body: I would rather you stayed says what the speaker prefers: that you stay. After would rather there can be a clause with its own subject, here you, and the verb in that clause takes a past-looking form, stayed, which has a remote, imagined feel rather than a past one. With a plain verb, as in I would rather stay, the person doing the staying is understood to be the speaker.
curious.try: Say what you would rather do tonight, then say what you would rather a friend did. How does the verb change?

teacher.summary: Explains would rather with a plain infinitival or a finite clause.
teacher.explain: Would rather expresses preference between actual or imagined alternatives. It can be followed by a plain infinitival or a finite subordinate clause. A finite clause can have its own subject and a modally remote preterite, as in I would rather you stayed. In I would rather stay, the subject of stay is understood as the matrix subject. This dictionary treats the pattern as a specialization of the VP and relates it to the irrealis were. It is provisional, with medium confidence.
teacher.terms: This dictionary describes would rather as a pattern followed by a plain infinitival or a finite subordinate clause.

contrasts.note: The subject of stay is understood as the speaker.
A finite clause with its own subject and a remote preterite.

watch_for: A learner might read stayed in I would rather you stayed as past time, though this dictionary describes it as modally remote.
A learner might take the subject of stay in I would rather stay to be someone other than the speaker.
teacher.activity: Pairs write five would-rather sentences about weekend plans, two with a plain verb and three with a clause having its own subject, then underline each verb form.

child.hook: How do you say what you want to do instead of something else?
child.explain: Would rather tells what you prefer. I would rather stay. You can also say what you want someone else to do. I would rather you stayed.
child.play: Tell a partner what you would rather do on a rainy day. Then say what you would rather a friend did.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Preference would rather." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/preference-would-rather-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
